title: CCATT to the Rescue
description:
Web Lead:
Critical situations call for #CriticalThinking. Airman First Class Thomas Barley introduces us to #TeamKadena's Critical Care Transport Team whose quick thinking is #SavingLives.

transcript.text: - [Reporter] In dire situations,
^cooperation and partnership
^can be the difference between life and death.
On Kadena, Navy and Air Force personnel
work together to gather equipment
that will help transfer a 16 month-old burn victim
from mainland Japan to a burn hospital in California.
- We are using equipment that's never before flown on a C-17
^We looked at everything else in the inventory
^and all our other options and realized
^it wasn't gonna work for the patient.
Normally when you're transporting small infants
who you're worried about thermo-regulation,
whether you can keep them warm,
whether you can keep the ambient humidity up.
This patient's a little older, greater than a year old,
so he wasn't going to fit in any of those options.
- And when you're out of options,
who better to ask for help but family.
Personnel had to think outside the box
and reach out to their sister services.
- Not only do we have multiple units coming together
to figure out a safe plan to transport this patient
but we have multiple service as well.
We wouldn't be able to take this piece of equipment
if the U.S. Naval Hospital in Okinawa
wasn't willing to release it to us for the mission.
So we have, not only multiple units,
but fairly joint service to make this happen.
- Working together, Air Force and Navy personnel
were able to lead the way in innovation,
accomplish the mission and change the way
future missions are carried out.
Airman First Class Thomas Barley, Kadena Air Base, Japan.
